title: 2026 U.S. House of Representatives Election — Utah's 1st Congressional District
description: For the first time since 2000, Salt Lake City falls into its own compact congressional district following court-ordered redistricting, creating an open seat in Utah's newly drawn 1st Congressional District. Incumbent Rep. Blake Moore (R) is running in the 2nd District instead, leaving a highly competitive race in a district with a Cook Partisan Voting Index of D+12. Republican nominee Riley Owen, a former White House staffer and Navy Reserve intelligence officer, will face the winner of a four-way Democratic primary featuring former U.S. Rep. Ben McAdams, state Sen. Nate Blouin, convention winner Liban Mohamed, and progressive tax attorney Michael Farrell. Libertarian candidate Jesse West will also appear on the November general election ballot.

candidates.name: Riley Owen
candidates.summary: Riley Owen is the Republican nominee for Utah's 1st Congressional District, having won the party nomination outright at the April 2026 Utah GOP convention with 71.2% of the delegate vote. He is a Naval Reserve intelligence officer and former White House staffer who focused on industrial policy, and his campaign emphasizes affordability, housing, paid family leave tax credits, and a pragmatic conservative approach to governing.

summary_sources.title: Riley Owen is the Utah GOP's man in the new 1st district. Can he win?

candidates.name: Jesse West
candidates.summary: Jesse West is the Libertarian Party candidate for Utah's 1st Congressional District. A 30-year-old family law attorney and chair of the Salt Lake City Libertarian Party, he campaigned on a platform of ending forever wars, abolishing the federal death penalty, reforming immigration with legal pathways, and legalizing cannabis. His campaign slogan is 'A vote for me is a vote to Ski not War.'

candidates.name: Ben McAdams
candidates.summary: Ben McAdams is a former U.S. Representative for Utah's 4th Congressional District (2019–2021), former Salt Lake County Mayor (2013–2019), and former Utah State Senator. He is the most recent Democrat to represent Utah in Congress and is widely considered the more centrist establishment candidate in the Democratic primary field for the open 1st District seat.

candidates.name: Liban Mohamed
candidates.summary: Liban Mohamed is a 27-year-old political newcomer and the son of Somali immigrants, born and raised in Utah. He won the April 2026 Utah Democratic Party nominating convention with 51.5% of delegate support after five rounds of ranked-choice voting, defeating former Congressman Ben McAdams. Mohamed has worked in public policy at the American Heart Association and in tech policy at Meta and TikTok, and he campaigns on progressive priorities including Medicare for All and data center regulation to protect the Great Salt Lake.

candidates.name: Nate Blouin
candidates.summary: Nate Blouin is a Utah State Senator representing District 13 (parts of Salt Lake County) since 2023, and is a progressive Democrat endorsed by Sen. Bernie Sanders. A climate policy advocate with a Master of Public Administration from Brown University, Blouin has focused on clean energy, affordable housing, and environmental justice. He has pledged to exit the primary race if polling shows another progressive candidate has stronger support, in an effort to consolidate the progressive vote.

candidates.name: Michael Farrell
candidates.summary: Michael Farrell is a progressive Democrat and tax attorney with over 12 years of experience, running for Utah's 1st Congressional District. After gathering 7,000 signatures to qualify for the primary ballot, he campaigns on single-payer healthcare, a full ban on hyperscale data centers in Utah to protect the Great Salt Lake, and a Green New Deal-style clean energy transition. He moved to Utah in 2022 and is a relative newcomer to the state's political scene.

forecast.rationale: No public polling exists for this race, capping confidence at medium. However, structural indicators strongly favor Democrats: court-ordered redistricting created a compact Salt Lake City-centered district with a Cook PVI of D+12 — a strong Democratic lean for a U.S. House seat. The Democratic nominee is still unsettled (four-way primary featuring former Rep. Ben McAdams, convention winner Liban Mohamed, state Sen. Nate Blouin, and Michael Farrell), adding some uncertainty about general election electability. The Republican nominee, Riley Owen, is a well-credentialed former White House staffer and Navy Reserve intelligence officer who won his party's convention with 71.2%. Libertarian Jesse West will also appear on the ballot but is unlikely to be competitive. Despite the unsettled Democratic field and absence of polling, the D+12 baseline makes Democrats clear favorites in this open seat.
